# @mk-kit/ui 0.37.0 — full API reference

Generated from the library sources. Browsable version: https://mk-kit.dev/api · JSON: https://mk-kit.dev/api.json · Guides: https://mk-kit.dev/llms.txt

## Usage

```bash
ng add @mk-kit/ui
```

Every component and directive below is standalone — import the class from its entry point and list it in `imports`. Attribute selectors like `button[mkButton]` enhance native elements; element selectors render their own template. Inputs marked two-way are `model()` signals and accept `[(name)]`. Inputs are signal inputs: read them as `comp.name()` in TypeScript.

## @mk-kit/ui/core

68 exports. `import { … } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

### MkAnchoredPanel (directive)

Selector: `[mkAnchoredPanel]` · exportAs: `mkAnchoredPanel`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/core-services

Import: `import { MkAnchoredPanel } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Anchored-overlay directive. Apply it to a floating panel element (a dropdown
list, calendar, menu, …) that is rendered inside its component's own template
— typically inside an `@if (open()) { … }` block. On init the directive
**teleports the panel to `document.body` and into the browser top layer** via
the native Popover API (`popover="manual"` + `showPopover()`), then positions
it against the anchor with `position: fixed`. Because the element stays part
of the component's Angular view, all bindings, `@for` content, events and
projected content keep working after the move.

The top layer is immune to ancestor `overflow`, `transform` and `z-index`
stacking contexts, so the panel can never be clipped by a container or hidden
behind sibling content. Where the Popover API is unavailable the panel still
renders in a `document.body` portal with a `z-index` fallback.

```html
<ul #panel mkAnchoredPanel [mkAnchoredPanelFor]="trigger" [matchWidth]="true"
    (dismiss)="close()"> … </ul>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkAnchoredPanelFor` | `HTMLElement \| ElementRef<HTMLElement> \| undefined` | `undefined` | The trigger element to position against. |
| `anchorRect` | `{ x: number; y: number; } \| undefined` | `undefined` | Viewport-point anchor (e.g. a right-click position) — takes precedence. |
| `placement` | `MkPlacement` | `'bottom-start'` | Preferred placement relative to the anchor. |
| `gap` | `number` | `4` | Distance in px between the anchor and the panel. |
| `matchWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Set the panel's `min-width` to the anchor's width (dropdowns). |
| `flip` | `boolean` | `true` | Flip to the opposite side when the preferred side would overflow. |
| `clamp` | `boolean` | `true` | Clamp the panel inside the viewport. |
| `keepOpenWhen` | `((target: Node) => boolean) \| null` | `null` | Predicate consulted before an outside pointerdown dismisses the panel. Return `true` for targets that must keep it open — e.g. a nested panel (a submenu) that lives in the top layer outside this element. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dismiss` | `void` | Emitted on an outside pointerdown or when the window loses focus. |

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `position(track?: boolean): void` | Recompute and apply the panel position. Safe to call at any time. With `track` (scroll-driven), the panel follows the anchor unclamped and dismisses once the anchor leaves the viewport (matching the CDK's reposition-with-auto-close scroll behaviour). |

### MkBreakpointService (service)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/core-services

Import: `import { MkBreakpointService } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Reactive viewport breakpoints, one `matchMedia` listener per step.

```ts
private readonly bp = inject(MkBreakpointService);
readonly compact = this.bp.down('md');          // Signal<boolean>
readonly columns = computed(() => this.bp.resolve({ xs: 1, md: 2, xl: 4 }));
```

On the server (no `window`) everything reports `xs`.

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `up(bp: MkBreakpoint): Signal<boolean>` | True while the viewport is at least `bp` wide (`up('md')` = md, lg, xl, 2xl). |
| `down(bp: MkBreakpoint): Signal<boolean>` | True while the viewport is narrower than `bp` (`down('md')` = xs, sm). |
| `between(from: MkBreakpoint, to: MkBreakpoint): Signal<boolean>` | True while the viewport is at least `from` and narrower than `to`. |
| `observe(query: string): Signal<boolean>` | Any media query as a signal, e.g. `observe('(orientation: portrait)')`. |
| `resolve<T>(value: MkResponsive<T>): T \| undefined` | Pick the entry of a responsive value for the current viewport — mobile-first, so `{ xs: 1, md: 2 }` gives 1 on `sm` and 2 on `xl`. A plain value is returned as is. Read inside a `computed` to track it. |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `breakpoints` | `MkBreakpoints` | The breakpoint scale in effect (see `MK_BREAKPOINTS`). |
| `current` | `Signal<MkBreakpoint>` | The widest breakpoint the viewport currently satisfies. |

### MkLiveAnnouncer (service)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/core-services

Import: `import { MkLiveAnnouncer } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Announces messages to assistive technology via a visually-hidden
`aria-live` region. Used by toasts, form validation, sort changes, etc.
so state changes are perceivable without sight. WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages).

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `announce(message: string, politeness?: MkAriaLivePoliteness): void` | Announce `message`. `politeness` controls interruption behavior. |

### MkOverlayService (service)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/core-services

Import: `import { MkOverlayService } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Lightweight, dependency-free overlay renderer. Instantiates a standalone
component into a body-level host, manages the backdrop, focus trapping,
Escape handling, and scroll locking. Powers Dialog, Menu, and others.

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `closeAll(): void` | Close every open overlay, newest first. Each is closed with no result, so `afterClosed` resolves undefined exactly as a backdrop click or Escape would. Safe to call when nothing is open. |
| `open<TComponent, TResult = unknown, TData = unknown>(component: Type<TComponent>, config?: MkOverlayConfig<TData>): MkOverlayRef<TResult, TComponent>` |  |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `openCount` | `number` | How many overlays are currently open. |

### MkThemeService (service)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/core-services

Import: `import { MkThemeService } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Reactive theme controller for mk-kit.

- `preference()` is the user's choice: `light`, `dark`, or `system`.
- `resolvedTheme()` is the concrete theme currently applied.
- Writes `data-mk-theme` on `<html>` and persists the choice to
  `localStorage`. When set to `system`, it live-tracks the OS setting and
  removes the attribute so pure-CSS `prefers-color-scheme` takes over.

Provided in root — inject it anywhere and bind to the signals.

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `setDensity(density: MkDensity): void` | Set the global density mode. |
| `toggleDensity(): void` | Toggle between comfortable and compact — the two modes a density switch in a UI offers. `touch` is a deliberate choice for a specific screen, not something to land on by toggling, so from `touch` this returns to comfortable rather than cycling. |
| `setTheme(preference: MkThemePreference): void` | Set the theme preference explicitly. |
| `toggle(): void` | Toggle between light and dark (resolving `system` first). |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `preference` | `Signal<MkThemePreference>` | The user's theme preference. |
| `resolvedTheme` | `Signal<MkResolvedTheme>` | The concrete theme in effect (`light` or `dark`). |
| `isDark` | `Signal<boolean>` | Convenience boolean for template bindings. |
| `density` | `Signal<MkDensity>` | The global density mode. `compact` tightens control heights and the core spacing steps via the `data-mk-density` attribute, `touch` enlarges them — every component follows automatically because they read the same tokens.  This signal is the GLOBAL mode only. To make one screen or dialog touch- sized inside an otherwise comfortable app, put `data-mk-density="touch"` on that element instead; the tokens inherit and this service stays out of it. |

### MkFieldContext (class)

Import: `import { MkFieldContext } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Field context — the contract a field wrapper (`mk-form-field`) exposes to
the control nested inside it. Controls inject it optionally
(`inject(MkFieldContext, { optional: true })`) to adopt the wrapper's
control id and to reflect its required/error state and `aria-describedby`
wiring — without depending on the `@mk-kit/ui/forms` entry point.

`MkFormField` provides itself under this token; standalone usage (no
wrapper) simply yields `null`.

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `controlId` | `string` | Id for the nested interactive control — adopt on your control element. |
| `labelId` | `string` | Id of the field's label element, for `aria-labelledby`. |
| `size` | `Signal<MkSize>` | The field's visual size, mirrored onto the nested control. |
| `isRequired` | `Signal<boolean>` | Whether the field is required (explicitly or via the bound control). |
| `hasError` | `Signal<boolean>` | Whether the field currently shows an error. |
| `describedBy` | `Signal<string \| null>` | Space-separated id list for the nested control's `aria-describedby`, or `null` when there is nothing to describe. |

### MkFocusTrap (class)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/core-services

Import: `import { MkFocusTrap } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Traps keyboard focus within `root` (wrapping Tab / Shift+Tab), moves focus
inside on activation, and restores focus to the previously-focused element
on release. Essential for accessible modals/menus (WCAG 2.4.3, 2.1.2).

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `activate(initialFocus?: HTMLElement): void` | Activate the trap and move focus to the first focusable element (or root). |
| `release(): void` | Deactivate and restore focus to the trigger element. |

### MkOverlayRef (class)

Import: `import { MkOverlayRef } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Handle to an open overlay. Injected into the rendered component and returned
from `MkOverlayService.open`. Resolve the overlay by calling `close`.

The close result is exposed three ways so the handle fits whatever style the
calling code already uses — they all settle together:

- `result` — a signal, for template binding and signal-based components.
- `closed$` — an Observable that emits once and completes, for RxJS
  pipelines. A service that hands a dialog result back to its callers can
  return this directly instead of wrapping the promise in `from(...)`.
- `afterClosed` — a Promise, for `await` / `.then()`.

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `close(result?: TResult): void` | Close the overlay, optionally returning a result. |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `componentRef` | `ComponentRef<TComponent> \| undefined` | The rendered component instance (set by the service after creation). |
| `closed` | `Signal<boolean>` | Becomes `true` once the overlay has been dismissed. |
| `result` | `Signal<TResult \| undefined>` | The value passed to `close`, or `undefined` while open and for a dismissal (Escape / backdrop). Read `closed()` to tell "closed with no result" apart from "still open". |
| `afterClosed` | `Promise<TResult \| undefined>` | Resolves with the close result when the overlay is dismissed. |
| `closed$` | `Observable<TResult \| undefined>` | Emits the close result once, then completes. Subscribing after the overlay has already closed replays the result immediately, so a late subscriber never hangs. |

### mkComputeAnchoredPosition (function)

Import: `import { mkComputeAnchoredPosition } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Pure viewport-positioning maths shared by every anchored overlay
(`MkAnchoredPanel` and the tooltip). Given the anchor rect, the panel
size and the viewport size, returns the top/left for a `position: fixed`
panel — flipping to the opposite side when it would overflow and clamping
back inside the viewport.

```ts
function mkComputeAnchoredPosition(anchor: MkRectLike, panel: MkSize, viewport: MkSize, opts: MkAnchoredPositionOptions): MkAnchoredPosition
```

### mkFirstErrorMessage (function)

Import: `import { mkFirstErrorMessage } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Resolves the message for the first error on a control, mirroring how
`mat-error` shows one message at a time.

Lookup order per key: the field's `overrides`, then the i18n `validation`
table, then the error payload's own `message` string (so a custom validator
can carry its text), then the generic fallback. Keys are visited in the
order the validators put them on the control, so composing
`[Validators.required, Validators.email]` surfaces "required" while empty.

```ts
function mkFirstErrorMessage(errors: ValidationErrors | null | undefined, strings: MkValidationStrings, overrides?: MkErrorMessages): string | null
```

Returns the tabbable elements inside `root`, in DOM order.

function mkGetFocusable(root: HTMLElement): HTMLElement[]

### mkHighlightJson (function)

Import: `import { mkHighlightJson } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Highlight a JSON document. Recognises object keys, strings, numbers, the
`true`/`false`/`null` literals and structural punctuation. Invalid JSON is
still highlighted token-by-token (the editor validates separately).

```ts
function mkHighlightJson(src: string): string
```

### mkQueryToPredicate (function)

Import: `import { mkQueryToPredicate } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Compile a query into a row predicate for client-side filtering
(`rows.filter(mkQueryToPredicate(query, fields))`). Unfinished rules are
ignored, so a half-edited query never blanks the table.

```ts
function mkQueryToPredicate<T extends object = Record<string, unknown>>(group: MkQueryGroup, fields?: readonly MkQueryField[]): (row: T) => boolean
```

### mkQueryToText (function)

Import: `import { mkQueryToText } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Human-readable sentence for a query, e.g.
`(Name contains "ada" and Orders at least 10) or Status is any of Active, Invited`.

```ts
function mkQueryToText(group: MkQueryGroup, fields?: readonly MkQueryField[], i18n?: MkI18nStrings): string
```

### mkUniqueId (function)

Import: `import { mkUniqueId } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Generates a stable, unique DOM id for wiring `aria-*` relationships
(labels, descriptions, controls). Prefer this over `Math.random()` so
ids are deterministic within a render and SSR-safe.

```ts
function mkUniqueId(prefix?: string): string
```

### mkValidatorChange (function)

Import: `import { mkValidatorChange } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Re-validates the bound form control whenever a validator's inputs change.

A `Validator` whose constraints come from component inputs (`[min]`,
`[max]`, `[required]`, …) must tell Angular when those inputs change,
otherwise the control keeps the verdict computed under the old constraints.
`NgModel`/`FormControlName` pass a callback to `registerOnValidatorChange`
for exactly this; call it from an effect over the constraint signals.

Must be called from an injection context (i.e. as a field initialiser).

```ts
private readonly validatorChange = mkValidatorChange(() => {
  this.min();
  this.max();
});

registerOnValidatorChange(fn: () => void): void {
  this.validatorChange.register(fn);
}
```

```ts
function mkValidatorChange(deps: () => void): MkValidatorChangeRef
```

### provideMkI18n (function)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/core-services

Import: `import { provideMkI18n } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Provide localised strings (merged over the English defaults) — pass any
subset. The nested `dateNames`, `blockEditor` and `validation` groups are
merged deeply, so partial overrides of those work too.

```ts
bootstrapApplication(App, {
  providers: [provideMkI18n({ noResults: 'Brak wyników', close: 'Zamknij' })],
});
```

```ts
function provideMkI18n(overrides: Partial<Omit<MkI18nStrings, "dateNames" | "blockEditor" | "validation">> & { dateNames?: Partial<MkDateNames>; blockEditor?: Partial<MkBlockEditorStrings>; validation?: Partial<MkValidationStrings>; }): Provider
```

### MK_I18N (token)

Import: `import { MK_I18N } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

The active string map. Defaults to `MK_DEFAULT_I18N`; override with
`provideMkI18n`. Inject it (`inject(MK_I18N)`) wherever a built-in
string is rendered.

```ts
const MK_I18N: InjectionToken<MkI18nStrings>;
```

### MkDateNames (interface)

Import: `import { MkDateNames } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Localised date-name tables consumed by the calendar, the date/month/week
pickers and `formatDate`. All arrays are full-length (12 months, 7 weekdays
starting with Sunday) — override the whole set for a locale.

Members:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `months` | `readonly string[]` | Full month names, January-first (12). |
| `monthsShort` | `readonly string[]` | Abbreviated month names (12). |
| `weekdays` | `readonly string[]` | Full weekday names, Sunday-first (7). |
| `weekdaysShort` | `readonly string[]` | Abbreviated weekday names (7). |
| `weekdaysNarrow` | `readonly string[]` | One/two-letter weekday names for calendar headers (7). |

### MkI18nStrings (interface)

Import: `import { MkI18nStrings } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

All user-facing strings the library renders itself (aria-labels, empty-state
text, control captions and screen-reader announcements). Consumers localise
the library by overriding any subset via `provideMkI18n`. Interpolated
strings are functions so translators control word order.

| Name | Type | Description |

### MkOverlayConfig (interface)

Import: `import { MkOverlayConfig } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Members:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data`? | `TData \| undefined` | Arbitrary data injected via `MK_OVERLAY_DATA`. |
| `hasBackdrop`? | `boolean \| undefined` | Render a dimmed scrim behind the panel. Default `true`. |
| `closeOnBackdropClick`? | `boolean \| undefined` | Close when the backdrop is clicked. Default `true`. |
| `closeOnEscape`? | `boolean \| undefined` | Close when Escape is pressed. Default `true`. |
| `trapFocus`? | `boolean \| undefined` | Trap focus within the panel and restore it on close. Default `true`. |
| `autoFocus`? | `boolean \| undefined` | Move focus to the panel's first focusable element on open. Default `true`. Set `false` to focus the panel itself instead — for content-led surfaces (a product sheet, a preview) where focusing the close button first reads as "dismiss me". Tab containment and focus restore are unaffected; turn `trapFocus` off only if you want neither. |
| `panelClass`? | `string \| string[] \| undefined` | Extra class(es) applied to the panel host element. |
| `role`? | `"dialog" \| "alertdialog" \| "menu" \| "listbox" \| undefined` | Accessible role for the panel. Default `dialog`. |
| `ariaLabel`? | `string \| undefined` | `aria-label` for the panel when no visible title is wired up. |
| `injector`? | `Injector \| undefined` | A custom injector to use as the parent for the rendered component. |

### MkQueryField (interface)

| --- | --- | --- |

| `type`? | `MkQueryValueType \| undefined` | Default `string`. |
| `options`? | `readonly MkQueryFieldOption[] \| undefined` | Choices for `select` fields. |
| `operators`? | `readonly MkQueryOperator[] \| undefined` | Restrict / reorder the operators offered (default: all for the type). |
| `placeholder`? | `string \| undefined` | Placeholder of the value editor. |

### MkQueryRule (interface)

Import: `import { MkQueryRule } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

A leaf condition. `value` is `[from, to]` for `between`, an array for `in` / `notIn`, absent for `empty` / `notEmpty`. Dates are ISO strings.

Members:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  |
| `field` | `string` |  |
| `operator` | `MkQueryOperator` |  |
| `value`? | `unknown` |  |

### MkValidationStrings (interface)

Import: `import { MkValidationStrings } from '@mk-kit/ui/core';`

Messages rendered by `mk-form-field` for the validation errors the library's
own controls produce, plus the standard Angular `Validators` keys, so a
field wrapping any control shows something sensible without per-form wiring.

Keys match the `ValidationErrors` keys exactly and each entry receives that
key's error payload. Override any subset through
`provideMkI18n({ validation: … })`, or a whole map per field via
`mk-form-field`'s `errorMessages` input.

Members:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | `string` | `Validators.required` — also emitted by checkbox and radio-group. |
| `email` | `string` | `Validators.email`. |
| `min` | `(err: { min: number; actual: number; }) => string` | `Validators.min`, and the numeric controls' `[min]`. |
| `max` | `(err: { max: number; actual: number; }) => string` | `Validators.max`, and the numeric controls' `[max]`. |
| `minlength` | `(err: { requiredLength: number; actualLength: number; }) => string` | `Validators.minLength` — also emitted by password-input and OTP. |
| `maxlength` | `(err: { requiredLength: number; actualLength: number; }) => string` | `Validators.maxLength`. |
| `pattern` | `string` | `Validators.pattern`. |
| `mkMinDate` | `(err: { min: Date; actual: Date; }) => string` | A date/month/week picker's `[min]`. |
| `mkMaxDate` | `(err: { max: Date; actual: Date; }) => string` | A date/month/week picker's `[max]`. |
| `mkDateFilter` | `string` | A date rejected by a calendar's `[disabledDate]` predicate. |
| `mkDateRangeIncomplete` | `string` | A range picker with only one end filled in. |
| `mkMinTime` | `(err: { min: string; actual: string; }) => string` | The time-picker's `[min]`. |
| `mkMaxTime` | `(err: { max: string; actual: string; }) => string` | The time-picker's `[max]`. |
| `mkMaxItems` | `(err: { max: number; actual: number; }) => string` | More items than a multi-select's, tag-input's or upload's `[max*]` allows. |
| `mkFileSize` | `(err: { max: number; maxLabel: string; name: string; }) => string` | A file larger than a file-upload's `[maxSize]`. |
| `mkFileType` | `(err: { accept: string; name: string; }) => string` | A file not matching a file-upload's `[accept]` filter. |
| `cardNumber` | `string` | A card number failing the Luhn checksum. |
| `iban` | `(err: { country: string; expectedLength: number \| null; }) => string` | An IBAN failing the mod-97 checksum. |
| `postalCode` | `(err: { country: string; example: string; }) => string` | A postal code not matching the country's format. |
| `taxId` | `(err: { country: string; label: string; example: string; }) => string` | A tax identifier not matching the country's format or checksum. |
| `unknown` | `string` | Fallback for an error key with no message of its own. |

## @mk-kit/ui/icon

6 exports. `import { … } from '@mk-kit/ui/icon';`

### MkIcon (component)

Selector: `mk-icon`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/icon

Import: `import { MkIcon } from '@mk-kit/ui/icon';`

Icon — renders a registered SVG by `name`, or your own projected `<svg>`.
The glyph inherits the current text colour (`currentColor`) and scales to the
`size` box, so it composes cleanly inside buttons, inputs and menus.

Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`); pass `label` to expose it as an image
to assistive tech.

```html
<mk-icon name="search" />
<mk-icon name="trash" size="lg" label="Delete" />
<button mkButton iconOnly aria-label="Menu"><mk-icon name="menu" /></button>
<mk-icon><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">…custom…</svg></mk-icon>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `''` | Name of a registered icon (see `MkIconRegistry`). |
| `size` | `number \| MkSize` | `'md'` | Size: `sm`/`md`/`lg`, or a pixel number for a custom dimension. |
| `label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name. When set the icon becomes `role="img"`; otherwise hidden. |

### MkIconRegistry (service)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/icon

Import: `import { MkIconRegistry } from '@mk-kit/ui/icon';`

IconRegistry — the name → SVG store behind `<mk-icon name="…">`. The built-in
sets — the hand-made `MK_DEFAULT_ICONS` and the Lucide-derived
`MK_EXTENDED_ICONS` — are registered on construction; add your own SVGs
(from a sprite, a design export, anything) with `register` /
`registerIcons`.

SVG markup is trusted verbatim (bypassed through `DomSanitizer`), so only
register icons from sources you control — never user input.

```ts
const reg = inject(MkIconRegistry);
reg.register('logo', '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">…</svg>');
reg.registerIcons({ save: '<svg…>', share: '<svg…>' });
```

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `register(name: string, svg: string): this` | Register (or overwrite) a single named icon from raw SVG markup. |
| `registerIcons(icons: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): this` | Register many icons at once from a `{ name: svg }` map. |
| `registerAliases(aliases: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): this` | Register alternative names that resolve to existing icons — e.g. map Material Symbols ligature names onto the built-in set (`{ delete: 'trash', expand_more: 'chevron-down' }`). A real icon registered under an alias name always wins over the alias. |
| `get(name: string): SafeHtml \| null` | Sanitized SVG for a name (aliases resolved), or `null` when unknown. |
| `has(name: string): boolean` | Whether an icon with this name (or alias) is registered. |
| `names(): string[]` | All registered icon names (useful for a picker / catalogue). |

### provideMkMaterialIcons (function)

Import: `import { provideMkMaterialIcons } from '@mk-kit/ui/icon';`

Installs the Material Symbols name aliases into the `MkIconRegistry`,
so `<mk-icon name="delete" />`, `name="expand_more"`, `name="visibility"`
etc. resolve to the built-in set. Add it to your bootstrap providers when
migrating an app off `<mat-icon>` ligatures:

```ts
bootstrapApplication(App, {
  providers: [provideMkMaterialIcons()],
});
```

```ts
function provideMkMaterialIcons(): EnvironmentProviders
```

### MK_DEFAULT_ICONS (const)

Import: `import { MK_DEFAULT_ICONS } from '@mk-kit/ui/icon';`

Name → SVG markup map of the default icons.

```ts
const MK_DEFAULT_ICONS: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
```

### MK_EXTENDED_ICONS (const)

Import: `import { MK_EXTENDED_ICONS } from '@mk-kit/ui/icon';`

Name → SVG markup map of the Lucide-derived icons registered by default.

```ts
const MK_EXTENDED_ICONS: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
```

### MK_MATERIAL_ICON_ALIASES (const)

Import: `import { MK_MATERIAL_ICON_ALIASES } from '@mk-kit/ui/icon';`

Material Symbols ligature names → built-in mk icon names. Lets templates
written against `<mat-icon>delete</mat-icon>` conventions keep their icon
names when migrating: `<mk-icon name="delete" />` renders the `trash`
glyph once `provideMkMaterialIcons` is installed.

Several Material names intentionally collapse onto one mk glyph (all the
calendar variants → `calendar`, the delete variants → `trash`, …). Names
not listed here have no sensible built-in equivalent — register your own
SVG under the Material name via `MkIconRegistry.register`.

```ts
const MK_MATERIAL_ICON_ALIASES: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
```

## @mk-kit/ui/checkbox

### MkCheckbox (component)

Selector: `mk-checkbox` · form control (ControlValueAccessor)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/toggles

Import: `import { MkCheckbox } from '@mk-kit/ui/checkbox';`

Checkbox — a themed checkbox built on a visually-hidden native
`input[type=checkbox]` (so keyboard + form semantics are native) with a
custom box. Supports an `indeterminate` state and projects its label.

Implements `ControlValueAccessor` with a two-way `checked` model, so it works
with `[(ngModel)]`, reactive forms and `[(checked)]`.

```html
<mk-checkbox [(ngModel)]="accepted">Accept terms</mk-checkbox>
<mk-checkbox [(checked)]="all" [indeterminate]="some()" tone="success">
  Select all
</mk-checkbox>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checked` (two-way) | `boolean` | `false` | Two-way checked state. |
| `indeterminate` (two-way) | `boolean` | `false` | Two-way indeterminate ("mixed") state; cleared when the user toggles. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable the control. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Force the invalid visual + `aria-invalid` when used standalone. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Mark required (adds `aria-required`). |
| `size` | `MkSize` | `'md'` | Control size. |
| `tone` | `MkTone` | `'primary'` | Semantic color tone for the checked box. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible label when no text content is projected. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checkedChange` | `boolean` | Emits when `checked` changes (two-way binding). |
| `indeterminateChange` | `boolean` | Emits when `indeterminate` changes (two-way binding). |

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `validate(control: AbstractControl): ValidationErrors \| null` | Reports `required` for an unchecked box when `[required]` is set, so `required` on the element behaves like `Validators.requiredTrue`. |

## @mk-kit/ui/directives

### MkAutofocus (directive)

Selector: `[mkAutofocus]`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkAutofocus } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Focuses the host element once it renders. Handy for dialogs, drawers and

```html
<input mkInput mkAutofocus />

| `mkAutofocusDelay` | `number` | `0` | Delay before focusing, in ms (e.g. to wait out an entrance animation). |

### MkAutosize (directive)

Grows a `<textarea>` to fit its content, between `minRows` and `maxRows`

| `mkAutosizeMaxRows` | `number` | `0` | Maximum height in rows before scrolling (0 = unbounded). |
| `mkAutosizeValue` | `unknown` | `undefined` | Bind the textarea's value so programmatic changes trigger a resize. |

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `resize(): void` | Recompute the textarea height from its content. |

### MkCan (directive)

Selector: `[mkCan]`

Import: `import { MkCan } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Structural directive that renders its template only while the app's
`MkPermissionPolicy` grants the given permission. With a
signal-based policy the check is live — the view is created and destroyed
as permissions change. When no policy is provided, everything is granted.

```html
<button *mkCan="'posts.delete'" (click)="remove()">Delete</button>

<!-- With a fallback template, like *ngIf's else: -->
<section *mkCan="'billing.view'; else locked">…</section>
<ng-template #locked><mk-empty-state title="No access" /></ng-template>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkCan` (required) | `string` |  | The permission key to check, e.g. `'posts.delete'`. |
| `mkCanElse` | `TemplateRef<unknown> \| null` | `null` | Template rendered while the permission is denied (`; else ref`). |

### MkCanDisable (directive)

Selector: `[mkCanDisable]`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkCanDisable } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Disables the host while the app's `MkPermissionPolicy` denies the
given permission — the "keep it visible but inert" alternative to `*mkCan`
for buttons, inputs and menu items.

While denied, the host gets `aria-disabled="true"`, and — when the element
supports it (button, input, select, textarea, fieldset…) — its native
`disabled` property is set too. Non-disableable elements (links, custom
menu items) get `aria-disabled` only; pair it with CSS / a click guard as
needed. The directive owns the disabled state: it also re-enables the host
when the permission is granted. With a signal-based policy the state flips
live; with no policy provided, everything is granted.

```html
<button [mkCanDisable]="'posts.delete'" (click)="remove()">Delete</button>
<a [mkCanDisable]="'billing.view'" routerLink="/billing">Billing</a>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkCanDisable` (required) | `string` |  | The permission key to check, e.g. `'posts.delete'`. |

### MkCannot (directive)

Selector: `[mkCannot]`

Import: `import { MkCannot } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

The negation of `MkCan`: renders its template only while the
permission is **denied** — for upsell hints, "ask an admin" notes and the
like. With no policy provided everything is granted, so `*mkCannot`
renders nothing.

```html
<p *mkCannot="'reports.export'">Exporting requires an admin role.</p>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkCannot` (required) | `string` |  | The permission key to check. |
| `mkCannotElse` | `TemplateRef<unknown> \| null` | `null` | Template rendered while the permission is granted (`; else ref`). |

### MkClickOutside (directive)

Selector: `[mkClickOutside]` · exportAs: `mkClickOutside`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkClickOutside } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Emits when a pointer press lands outside the host element — the building block
for dismissing menus, popovers and custom dropdowns. Listens on the document
in the capture phase so it fires before the target handles the event.

```html
<div class="panel" (mkClickOutside)="close()">…</div>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkClickOutsideEnabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Disable the listener without removing the directive. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mkClickOutside` | `PointerEvent` | Emits the originating event when a pointerdown occurs outside the host. |

### MkCopyToClipboard (directive)

Selector: `[mkCopyToClipboard]` · exportAs: `mkCopyToClipboard`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkCopyToClipboard } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Copies text to the clipboard when the host is clicked. Emits `(copied)` on
success and `(copyFailed)` on error, and exposes a transient `copied` signal
(via `exportAs`) so a template can show a "Copied!" state without extra code.

```html
<button mkButton [mkCopyToClipboard]="token" #c="mkCopyToClipboard">
  {{ c.justCopied() ? 'Copied!' : 'Copy' }}
</button>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkCopyToClipboard` (required) | `string` |  | The text to copy. |
| `mkCopyFeedbackDuration` | `number` | `1500` | How long (ms) the `copied` signal stays true after a successful copy. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `copied` | `string` | Emits the copied text on success. |
| `copyFailed` | `unknown` | Emits the error on failure. |

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `copy(): Promise<void>` | Copy the text now. Bound to the host click, but callable directly too. |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `justCopied` | `Signal<boolean>` | True for `feedbackDuration` ms after a successful copy. |

### MkField (directive)

Selector: `[mkField]`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/text-inputs

Import: `import { MkField } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Field — applies the semantic mobile-keyboard and autofill attribute bundle
for a kind of field, so you never again ship an email input that iOS
capitalises or an address input the browser can't autofill.

It sets `type`, `inputmode`, `autocomplete`, `autocapitalize`, `autocorrect`,
`spellcheck` and `enterkeyhint` (see `MK_FIELD_PRESETS`) and nothing
else — no styling, no value handling — so it composes with `mkInput`,
`mk-form-field`, `[(ngModel)]` and reactive forms untouched.

```html
<input mkInput mkField="email" formControlName="email" />
<input mkInput mkField="street" formControlName="street" />
<input mkInput [mkField]="isCompany() ? 'organization' : 'name'" />
```

## Precedence

A **static** attribute you write on the element wins: the directive reads the
seven attributes once at construction (before any host binding has run) and
keeps whatever was already there, filling in only what you left out. So
`<input mkField="username" type="password" />` stays a password field but
still gets `autocomplete="username"`, `autocapitalize="off"`, …

A **template binding** for the same attribute (`[attr.autocomplete]="…"`)
does *not* win — Angular applies directive host bindings after template
bindings, so the preset overwrites it. Use a static attribute to override, or
drop `mkField` and set the bundle yourself.

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkField` (required) | `MkFieldKind` |  | Which kind of field this is. |

### MkHotkey (directive)

Selector: `[mkHotkey]` · exportAs: `mkHotkey`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkHotkey } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

`[mkHotkey]` — declaratively bind a keyboard shortcut to a host element.

When the combo fires, a `<button>` or `<a>` host is `click()`ed; any other
host emits `(mkHotkeyPressed)`. Registration is scoped to the element's
lifetime (auto-unregistered on destroy) via `MkHotkeysService`.

```html
<button mkHotkey="mod+s" (click)="save()">Save</button>
<div mkHotkey="?" (mkHotkeyPressed)="showHelp()">…</div>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkHotkey` (required) | `string` |  | The combo (or space-separated chord) to bind, e.g. `mod+k`, `g i`, `?`. |
| `mkHotkeyAllowInInput` | `boolean` | `false` | Fire even while an editable field is focused. |
| `mkHotkeyPreventDefault` | `boolean` | `true` | Call `preventDefault()` when the hotkey fires. Defaults to `true`. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mkHotkeyPressed` | `KeyboardEvent` | Emitted when the hotkey fires and the host is not a button/link. |

### MkInfiniteScroll (directive)

Selector: `[mkInfiniteScroll]` · exportAs: `mkInfiniteScroll`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkInfiniteScroll } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

InfiniteScroll — emits `(mkInfiniteScroll)` when the host scroll container is
scrolled within `distance` px of its bottom, so a list can load its next
page. Apply it to the scrollable element (`overflow: auto`). It fires once per
approach and re-arms after you scroll back up past the threshold, so a single
gesture never triggers repeated loads. Set `disabled` while a page is loading
or once everything is loaded.

```html
<div class="feed" mkInfiniteScroll [disabled]="loading() || done()"
     (mkInfiniteScroll)="loadMore()">

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `distance` | `number` | `200` | Distance (px) from the bottom at which the output fires. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Pause firing (e.g. while a page is loading or all items are loaded). |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mkInfiniteScroll` | `void` | Emitted when the host is scrolled near its bottom. |

### MkIntersect (directive)

Selector: `[mkIntersect]` · exportAs: `mkIntersect`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkIntersect } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Intersect — a thin `IntersectionObserver` wrapper. Emits `(mkIntersect)` with
the host's visibility whenever it enters or leaves the viewport (or `root`),
and exposes an `intersecting` signal via `exportAs`. Set `once` to fire a
single time and disconnect — the primitive for reveal-on-scroll animations
and lazy loading.

```html
<img [attr.src]="loaded() ? src : null" mkIntersect once
     (mkIntersect)="loaded.set(true)" />

<div mkIntersect #io="mkIntersect" [class.in-view]="io.intersecting()">…</div>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | `HTMLElement \| null` | `null` | Element used as the viewport for the check (defaults to the browser one). |
| `rootMargin` | `string` | `'0px'` | Margin grown/shrunk around the root before computing intersection. |
| `threshold` | `number \| number[]` | `0` | Visibility ratio(s) at which the observer fires. |
| `once` | `boolean` | `false` | Emit the first time the host becomes visible, then disconnect. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mkIntersect` | `boolean` | Emits the host's `isIntersecting` state on every change. |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `intersecting` | `WritableSignal<boolean>` | The current visibility, also readable via `exportAs`. |

### MkScrollspy (directive)

Selector: `[mkScrollspy]` · exportAs: `mkScrollspy`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkScrollspy } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Scrollspy — tracks which section is currently in view and exposes its `id`,
so a table of contents / "on this page" nav can highlight the active link.

Apply it to any element (typically the nav) and point `mkScrollspy` at a CSS
selector matching the section elements to watch (each needs an `id`). Read the
active id via the exported instance, or bind `(activeChange)`:

```html
<nav mkScrollspy="main :is(h2, h3)[id]" #spy="mkScrollspy">
  <a href="#intro" [class.is-active]="spy.activeId() === 'intro'">Intro</a>
  …
</nav>
```

A section activates once its top passes `offset` px below the top of the
scroll root (default the viewport). When scrolling through a gap between
sections the previous one stays active until the next crosses the line.

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkScrollspy` (required) | `string` |  | CSS selector for the section elements to track (queried within `root`). |
| `root` | `HTMLElement \| null` | `null` | Scroll container. Sections are queried inside it and its top edge is the activation reference. Defaults to the whole document / viewport. |
| `offset` | `number` | `96` | Distance (px) below the scroll root's top at which a section becomes active. Raise it to account for a sticky header. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activeChange` | `string \| null` | Emitted whenever the active section changes. |

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `refresh(): void` | Re-evaluate the active section (call after sections change). |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activeId` | `WritableSignal<string \| null>` | The id of the currently active section (`null` before the first one). |

### MkHistoryService (service)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/core-services

Import: `import { MkHistoryService } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

MkHistoryService — the app-wide `MkHistoryStack` singleton. Inject it
anywhere; call `MkHistoryStack.createScope` for an isolated local
stack, or wire `mod+z` / `mod+shift+z` / `mod+y` with
`registerHistoryHotkeys`.

### Recipe — undoable `mk-table` cell edits
Wire the table's `(cellEdit)` output so each saved cell becomes one
undoable step. Apply the edit yourself first (`push()` records an action
that already happened), and match rows by a stable id — the row object is
replaced by the immutable update:

```ts
// <mk-table [rows]="rows()" [columns]="columns" (cellEdit)="onCellEdit($event)" />
private readonly history = inject(MkHistoryService);
readonly rows = signal<Order[]>([...]);

onCellEdit(edit: MkCellEdit<Order>): void {
  const previous = edit.row[edit.key as keyof Order];
  const apply = (value: unknown) =>
    this.rows.update((rows) =>
      rows.map((r) => (r.id === edit.row.id ? { ...r, [edit.key]: value } : r)),
    );
  apply(edit.value); // first execution is the caller's job
  this.history.push({
    label: `Edit ${edit.key}`,
    undo: () => apply(previous),
    redo: () => apply(edit.value),
  });
}
```

Undoing replays the old value through the same `apply` function; if your
change pipeline re-emits into `onCellEdit` during that replay, the
re-entrancy guard drops the spurious `push()` (see `MkHistoryStack`).

### MkHotkeysService (service)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkHotkeysService } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

MkHotkeysService — app-wide keyboard shortcuts. Register a combo string and a
handler; a single `keydown` listener (attached lazily on the first
registration, browser only) dispatches to every match.

Supports single combos (`'mod+k'`, `'ctrl+shift+p'`, `'?'`) and simple
two-step chords (`'g i'`). By default hotkeys are ignored while an editable
field is focused — pass `allowInInput` to opt in per registration.

```ts
const off = hotkeys.register('mod+k', (e) => openPalette(), { preventDefault: true });
// …later
off();
```

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `register(combo: string, handler: (e: KeyboardEvent) => void, options?: MkHotkeyOptions): () => void` | Register `combo` → `handler`. Returns a disposer that unregisters it. `combo` may be a single combo or a space-separated two-step chord. |
| `unregisterAll(): void` | Remove every registration and detach the listener. |

### MkHistoryStack (class)

Import: `import { MkHistoryStack } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

MkHistoryStack — a pure, signal-based, linear undo/redo command stack with
no Angular DI involved. Instantiate it directly for a local editing session
(a dialog, a canvas, a form wizard), or use the app-wide singleton
`MkHistoryService`.

```ts
const stack = new MkHistoryStack();
deleteRow(row);                                  // 1. do the work yourself
stack.push({                                     // 2. record how to revert/redo it
  label: 'Delete row',
  undo: () => insertRow(row),
  redo: () => deleteRow(row),
});
stack.undo();                                    // row is back
```

### Linear history
`push()` clears the redo branch — after undoing twice and pushing a new
entry, the two undone entries are gone (the standard editor model).

### ⚠️ Re-entrancy guard — the classic footgun
Pushes made **while** `undo()` or `redo()` is executing are **silently
ignored**. Naive consumers often record history from a generic change
handler (`(cellEdit)`, `valueChanges`, …); when an undo replays the old
value, that same handler fires again and would push a mirror entry,
corrupting the stack into an undo/redo ping-pong. The guard makes that
pattern safe by construction. If you need to record something new in
response to an undo, do it after `undo()` returns.

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `push(entry: MkHistoryEntry): void` | Record an already-performed action. Clears the redo branch and evicts the oldest entry beyond `limit`. Ignored while `undo()`/`redo()` is executing (see the re-entrancy note on the class) — inside a `batch()` the entry is collected into the composite instead. |
| `undo(): boolean` | Undo the most recent entry. Returns `false` when there is nothing to undo. |
| `redo(): boolean` | Redo the most recently undone entry. Returns `false` when there is nothing to redo. |
| `clear(): void` | Drop all entries (both branches) and any in-flight batch collection. |
| `batch<T>(label: string, work: () => T): T` | Group every `push()` made during `work()` into **one** undoable step. Undo runs the children in reverse order; redo runs them forward. Nested `batch()` calls flatten into the outermost batch (its label wins). An empty batch records nothing. Returns `work()`'s result; if `work()` throws, entries pushed before the throw are still committed. |
| `createScope(): MkHistoryStack` | Create an **independent** stack with the same API — e.g. for a dialog's local editing session that should not pollute the app-wide history. Discard it (or `clear()` it) when the session ends. |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canUndo` | `Signal<boolean>` | True when at least one entry can be undone. |
| `canRedo` | `Signal<boolean>` | True when at least one undone entry can be redone. |
| `undoLabel` | `Signal<string \| null>` | Label of the entry `undo()` would revert, or `null` ("Undo *Delete row*"). |
| `redoLabel` | `Signal<string \| null>` | Label of the entry `redo()` would re-apply, or `null`. |
| `size` | `Signal<number>` | Number of undoable entries currently on the stack. |
| `limit` | `number` | Maximum number of undoable entries kept (default `100`). When exceeded the **oldest** entries are dropped. Settable at any time; lowering it trims the stack immediately. Values below 1 are clamped to 1. |

### MkPermissionPolicy (class)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/utilities

Import: `import { MkPermissionPolicy } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Permission policy — the contract the permission directives (`*mkCan`,
`*mkCannot`, `[mkCanDisable]`) check against. Provide an implementation
once at bootstrap; the directives inject it optionally and, when no policy
is provided at all, treat every permission as **granted** — an app that
never wires permissions must not have its whole UI hidden.

`can` may return a plain `boolean` (static role checks) or a
`Signal<boolean>` (live permissions). The directives normalise both, and a
signal-returning policy re-evaluates reactively: views appear/disappear and
controls enable/disable the moment the underlying permissions change.

```ts
// A signal-based policy fed from an auth service:

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `can(permission: string): boolean \| Signal<boolean>` | Whether the current user holds `permission`. Return a `Signal<boolean>` to make the verdict live; a plain boolean is treated as static. |

### mkApplyMask (function)

Import: `import { mkApplyMask } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Format `value` against a mask `pattern`. Pattern tokens: `0` = digit,
`A` = letter, `*` = alphanumeric; any other character is a literal that is
inserted automatically. Characters that don't fit the current token are
skipped, so pasted / mistyped input is coerced into shape.

Returns the `masked` (display) string and the `unmasked` string (only the
token characters — the value you usually store).

```ts
function mkApplyMask(value: string, pattern: string): MkMaskResult
```

### mkMaskCaret (function)

Import: `import { mkMaskCaret } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Compute where the caret belongs after re-masking: after the same number of
value (alphanumeric) characters the caret used to sit behind, absorbing any
literal(s) that immediately follow — so typing "1" in "(0)" lands the caret
after the "(". Shared by `MkMask` and the masked form controls.

```ts
function mkMaskCaret(oldValue: string, oldCaret: number, masked: string): number
```

### mkMatchesHotkey (function)

Import: `import { mkMatchesHotkey } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Does a `keydown` event satisfy a hotkey? `combo` may be a raw string (parsed
on the fly) or an already-parsed `MkParsedHotkey`.

The key is compared case-insensitively; modifier flags must match exactly.
`mod` resolves to Meta on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Shift is not enforced for
symbol keys (e.g. `'?'`), whose shifted state varies by keyboard layout.

```ts
function mkMatchesHotkey(event: KeyboardEvent, combo: string | MkParsedHotkey): boolean
```

### mkParseHotkey (function)

Import: `import { mkParseHotkey } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Parse a single hotkey combo (e.g. `'mod+k'`, `'ctrl+shift+p'`, `'?'`) into a
structured `MkParsedHotkey`. Tokens are joined by `+`; the last
non-modifier token is the trigger key. Pure and SSR-safe.

For a chord (space-separated sequence like `'g i'`), split on whitespace and
parse each step — `MkHotkeysService` does this for you.

```ts
function mkParseHotkey(combo: string): MkParsedHotkey
```

### mkPermissionGranted (function)

Import: `import { mkPermissionGranted } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Resolve a policy verdict to a boolean, unwrapping signal-based results.
Call it inside a reactive context (`computed` / `effect`) so a
signal-returning policy stays live. A missing policy grants everything.

```ts
function mkPermissionGranted(policy: MkPermissionPolicy | null, permission: string): boolean
```

### registerHistoryHotkeys (function)

Import: `import { registerHistoryHotkeys } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

Opt-in helper wiring the standard editor shortcuts to a history stack
through `MkHotkeysService`:

- `mod+z` → `undo()`
- `mod+shift+z` **and** `mod+y` → `redo()`

Must be called in an **injection context** (constructor, field initializer,
or `runInInjectionContext`). Nothing is registered automatically — apps own
their shortcuts and call this where (and if) they want them:

```ts
export class AppShell {
  private readonly disposeHistoryKeys = registerHistoryHotkeys();
}
```

Pass a specific stack (e.g. a `createScope()` stack for a dialog) to bind
the shortcuts to it instead of the app-wide `MkHistoryService`.

Returns a dispose function that unregisters all three shortcuts; it is also
called automatically when the current injection context is destroyed.

Notes:
- `MkHotkeysService` ignores keydowns while an editable element
  (input/textarea/select/contentEditable) is focused, so native text-field
  undo keeps working — no extra handling needed here.
- The shortcuts register with `preventDefault` so the browser's own
  history/document undo does not fire alongside yours.

```ts
function registerHistoryHotkeys(history?: MkHistoryStack): () => void
```

```

### MkHistoryEntry (interface)

Import: `import { MkHistoryEntry } from '@mk-kit/ui/directives';`

A single undoable step recorded in an `MkHistoryStack`.

The **first** execution of an action is the caller's job — `push()` records
an action that has *already happened*. `undo()` reverts it; `redo()` applies
it again after an undo.

Members:

| `label` | `string` | Human label for menus/tooltips ("Delete row", "Move card"). |
| `undo` | `(): void` | Revert the action. |
| `redo` | `(): void` | Re-apply the action after an undo. |

## @mk-kit/ui/dnd

9 exports. `import { … } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

### MkDrag (component)

Selector: `[mkDrag]` · exportAs: `mkDrag`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/drag-drop

Import: `import { MkDrag } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

Makes an item inside a `[mkDropList]` draggable — by pointer (mouse / touch /
pen) **and** by keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1). The item is focusable, exposes
`role="button"` + `aria-roledescription="Draggable item"`, and every move is
announced via `MkLiveAnnouncer`.

Keyboard: focus an item and press **Space/Enter** to pick it up, **Arrow**
keys to move it (crossing into connected lists at the ends / across the
perpendicular axis), **Space/Enter** to drop, **Escape** to cancel.

Touch: a swipe scrolls the page as usual — the drag only arms after a
long-press (`mkDragTouchDelay`, default 300 ms). While armed the item
gets the `mk-drag--armed` class so consumers can style the lift moment.
Mouse and pen drags start immediately, as before.

Performance: pointer moves are rAF-coalesced (one hit-test + one set of
style/DOM writes per frame) against list/item rects snapshotted when the
drag lifts, so a move never forces layout. The pending frame is flushed
synchronously on release so drops land exactly where the pointer ended.

```html
<li mkDrag [mkDragData]="row" [mkDragDisabled]="row.locked">
  <span mkDragHandle aria-hidden="true">⠿</span> {{ row.title }}
</li>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkDragData` | `T \| undefined` |  | Arbitrary payload associated with this item. |
| `mkDragDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable dragging this specific item. |
| `mkDragTouchDelay` | `number` | `300` | Long-press delay (ms) before a *touch* pointer arms the drag. Until it elapses a swipe scrolls natively; moving more than `TOUCH_SLOP` pixels abandons the pending drag. `0` arms immediately (legacy behavior). Mouse and pen are never delayed. |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `element` | `HTMLElement` | The item's host element. |
| `disabled` | `Signal<boolean>` | Effective disabled state (item- or list-level). |

### MkDropList (component)

Selector: `[mkDropList]` · exportAs: `mkDropList`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/drag-drop

Import: `import { MkDropList } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

A drop container for reorderable `[mkDrag]` items.

- **Sort list:** a single `[mkDropList]` over an array — items reorder within it.
- **Buckets / kanban:** several `[mkDropList]`s wired together with
  `mkDropListConnectedTo` so items transfer between them (both by pointer and
  by keyboard at the ends of a list).

The array bound to `mkDropListData` is **not** mutated for you — handle
`mkDropListDropped` and call `mkMoveItemInArray` / `mkTransferArrayItem`.

```html
<ul mkDropList [mkDropListData]="todo()"
    mkDropListId="todo" [mkDropListConnectedTo]="['done']"
    (mkDropListDropped)="drop($event)">

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mkDropListData` | `readonly T[]` | `[]` | The array backing the list. Bound, never mutated by the directive. |
| `mkDropListId` | `string \| undefined` |  | Stable id used to connect lists. Auto-generated when omitted. |
| `mkDropListConnectedTo` | `readonly string[]` | `[]` | Ids of other lists items may be transferred into. |
| `mkDropListLabel` | `string` | `''` | Human-readable name used in screen-reader announcements when an item is moved into this list (e.g. `"In progress"`). Falls back to the list `id` — which may be auto-generated gibberish — so set it wherever users can move items across lists by keyboard. |
| `mkDropListOrientation` | `MkDropListOrientation` | `'vertical'` | Layout axis; controls pointer hit-testing and arrow-key direction. |
| `mkDropListDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable dropping into (and dragging out of) this list. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mkDropListDropped` | `MkDropEvent<T>` | Fires when an item is dropped into this list (pointer or keyboard). |

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `size(): number` | Number of drag items currently in the list. |
| `indexOf(drag: MkDrag<any>): number` | Index of `drag` among this list's items, or -1. |
| `itemElementsExcept(exclude: MkDrag<any>): HTMLElement[]` | Host elements of this list's items, excluding `exclude`, in DOM order. |
| `setReceiving(value: boolean): void` | Toggle the "receiving" highlight (called by the active drag). |
| `emitDrop(event: MkDropEvent<any>): void` | Emit a drop into this list. Called by the active `MkDrag`. |

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `element` | `HTMLElement` | The list's host element (drop target bounds). |
| `id` | `Signal<string>` | Resolved id (input or generated). |
| `label` | `Signal<string>` | Announceable name: the label when set, otherwise the resolved id. |
| `connectedTo` | `Signal<readonly string[]>` | Connected-list ids, normalised to a plain array. |

### MkSortableList (component)

Selector: `mk-sortable-list`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/drag-drop

Import: `import { MkSortableList } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

Thin convenience wrapper over a single `[mkDropList]` for the common
"reorderable list" case. Bind `items` two-way and provide an `<ng-template>`
to render each row; drops are applied to the model for you (via
`mkMoveItemInArray`).

For connected buckets / kanban, use `[mkDropList]` + `[mkDrag]` directly.

```html
<mk-sortable-list [(items)]="rows">
  <ng-template let-row let-i="index">
    <span mkDragHandle aria-hidden="true">⠿</span> {{ i + 1 }}. {{ row.name }}
  </ng-template>
</mk-sortable-list>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (two-way) | `T[]` | `[]` | The ordered items (two-way). Reordered in place on drop. |
| `orientation` | `MkDropListOrientation` | `'vertical'` | Layout axis of the list. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable reordering. |
| `trackBy` | `(index: number, item: T) => unknown` | `(_, item) => item` | `@for` tracking function. Defaults to identity (track by item). |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `itemsChange` | `T[]` | Emits when `items` changes (two-way binding). |
| `sorted` | `MkDropEvent<T>` | Emitted after the model has been reordered. |

### MkDragHandle (directive)

Selector: `[mkDragHandle]` · exportAs: `mkDragHandle`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/drag-drop

Import: `import { MkDragHandle } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

Optional grip that restricts where a pointer drag of the enclosing
`[mkDrag]` may begin. Place it on the element the user should press to drag;
without any handle the whole item is draggable.

A directive (not a component), so it composes onto anything — a `<span>`,
a `<button>`, or another component's host such as `<mk-icon mkDragHandle />`.
Its look (grab cursor, muted colour, `touch-action: none`) ships as the
global `.mk-drag-handle` class in the theme stylesheet.

```html
<div mkDrag [mkDragData]="row">
  <span mkDragHandle aria-hidden="true">⠿</span>
  {{ row.name }}
</div>
```

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `element` | `HTMLElement` | The handle's host element. |

### MkDragDropRegistry (service)

Import: `import { MkDragDropRegistry } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

Central registry of every live `[mkDropList]` on the page, keyed by id.

Connected lists (kanban "buckets") use it to resolve the sibling lists named
in `mkDropListConnectedTo`, and both pointer and keyboard dragging use it to
find the group of lists an item may travel between.

Registration is automatic — you never call this service directly; it is
documented so tooling/tests can inspect the wiring.

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `register(id: string, list: MkDropList<any>): void` | Register (or replace) the list published under `id`. |
| `unregister(id: string, list: MkDropList<any>): void` | Remove `list` from the registry if it is still the holder of `id`. |
| `get(id: string): MkDropList<any> \| undefined` | Look up a list by its `mkDropListId`. |
| `all(): MkDropList<any>[]` | All registered lists, in registration order. |
| `connectedGroup(list: MkDropList<any>): MkDropList<any>[]` | The ordered travel group for `list`: `list` itself plus every enabled list it is `mkDropListConnectedTo`, in registration (roughly DOM) order. Used to resolve "adjacent" lists for keyboard column-to-column movement and to hit-test the pointer against candidate targets. |

### mkMoveItemInArray (function)

Import: `import { mkMoveItemInArray } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

Move an item within a single array from `fromIndex` to `toIndex`.
Mutates and returns `array`.

```ts
mkMoveItemInArray(rows, e.previousIndex, e.currentIndex);
```

```ts
function mkMoveItemInArray<T>(array: T[], fromIndex: number, toIndex: number): T[]
```

### mkTransferArrayItem (function)

Import: `import { mkTransferArrayItem } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

Move an item from one array (`from`) to another (`to`), removing it from
`from[fromIndex]` and inserting it at `to[toIndex]`. Mutates both arrays and
returns the target (`to`) array.

```ts
mkTransferArrayItem(todo, done, e.previousIndex, e.currentIndex);
```

```ts
function mkTransferArrayItem<T>(from: T[], to: T[], fromIndex: number, toIndex: number): T[]
```

### MkDropEvent (interface)

Import: `import { MkDropEvent } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

Emitted by `[mkDropList]` (`mkDropListDropped`) when an item is dropped.

Mirrors the shape of Angular CDK's `CdkDragDrop` so the exported
`mkMoveItemInArray` / `mkTransferArrayItem` helpers can be used
exactly as their CDK counterparts:

```ts
onDrop(e: MkDropEvent) {
  if (e.previousContainer === e.container) {
    mkMoveItemInArray(e.container.mkDropListData(), e.previousIndex, e.currentIndex);
  } else {
    mkTransferArrayItem(
      e.previousContainer.mkDropListData(),
      e.container.mkDropListData(),
      e.previousIndex, e.currentIndex,
    );
  }
}
```

Members:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `previousIndex` | `number` | Index of the item within `previousContainer`'s data before the drop. |
| `currentIndex` | `number` | Index the item should occupy within `container`'s data after the drop. |
| `item` | `MkDrag<T>` | The `MkDrag` directive instance that was moved. |
| `previousContainer` | `MkDropList<T>` | The list the item came from. |
| `container` | `MkDropList<T>` | The list the item was dropped into (same as `previousContainer` for a re-sort). |
| `isPointerEvent` | `boolean` | `true` for pointer (mouse/touch/pen) drops, `false` for keyboard drops. |

### MkDropListOrientation (type)

Import: `import { MkDropListOrientation } from '@mk-kit/ui/dnd';`

Layout axis a drop list lays its items along.

```ts
type MkDropListOrientation = 'vertical' | 'horizontal';
```

### MkDrawer (component)

    <button mkButton (click)="apply()">Apply</button>
  </div>
</mk-drawer>
```

| `hasBackdrop` | `boolean` | `true` | Render a dimmed backdrop and lock body scroll (modal). |
| `closeOnBackdrop` | `boolean` | `true` | Close when the backdrop is clicked. |
| `closeOnEscape` | `boolean` | `true` | Close on the Escape key. |
| `trapFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Trap Tab focus inside the panel while open. |
| `heading` | `string` | `''` | Optional heading rendered in the header. |
| `hideClose` | `boolean` | `false` | Hide the header close button. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name when no `heading` is provided. |
