```ts
type MkDynamicFieldType = | 'text' | 'email' | 'password' | 'url' | 'tel' | 'search' | 'textarea' | 'number' | 'currency' | 'date' | 'time' | 'datetime' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'autocomplete' | 'radio' | 'toggle' | 'checkbox' | 'switch' | 'slider' | 'rating' | 'color' | 'tags' | 'phone' | 'file' | 'code' | 'custom';
```

## @mk-kit/ui/media

20 exports. `import { … } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

### MkImage (component)

Selector: `mk-image` · exportAs: `mkImage`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/images

Import: `import { MkImage } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Image — an enhanced image block. While the picture loads it shows a skeleton
shimmer, and when loading fails it swaps to a localised fallback panel
(icon + text, never colour alone). The picture is wrapped in a `<figure>`
with an optional `<figcaption>`, and changing `src` restarts the whole load
cycle.

```html
<mk-image
  src="/photos/harbour.jpg"
  alt="Harbour at dawn"
  aspectRatio="16 / 9"
  caption="The old harbour, photographed at dawn"
  (loaded)="onLoaded()"
  (errored)="onErrored()"
/>

<!-- The hero: eager, high priority, and sized per breakpoint so a phone
     does not download the desktop file. -->
<mk-image
  src="/photos/hero-1600.jpg"
  srcset="/photos/hero-800.jpg 800w, /photos/hero-1600.jpg 1600w"
  sizes="100vw"
  alt=""
  aspectRatio="16 / 9"
  priority
/>
```

`aspectRatio` is what keeps this from shifting layout: the frame reserves
its box before the picture arrives, so nothing below it moves.

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` (required) | `string` |  | Image URL. Changing it resets the block to its loading state. |
| `alt` | `string` | `''` | Alt text, always reflected onto the `<img>`. Keep `''` for decorative images. |
| `aspectRatio` | `string` | `'auto'` | Any CSS `aspect-ratio` value for the frame, e.g. `'1 / 1'` or `'16 / 9'`. |
| `fit` | `MkImageFit` | `'cover'` | How the picture fills the frame. |
| `rounded` | `MkImageRounded` | `'md'` | Corner rounding of the frame. |
| `caption` | `string` | `''` | Caption rendered in a `<figcaption>` below the picture. |
| `lazy` | `boolean` | `true` | Defer fetching until near the viewport (`loading="lazy"` vs `"eager"`). |
| `priority` | `boolean` | `false` | Mark this as the page's LCP image: fetched eagerly at high priority and decoded synchronously, and `lazy` is ignored. Use it on exactly ONE image per page — the hero. Marking several is worse than marking none, because they then compete for the same bandwidth the real LCP image needs.  This does NOT emit a `<link rel=preload>`; the tag has to be in the HTML the server sends to beat the preload scanner, which a component rendered later cannot guarantee. Pair it with a preload hint for a background or late-rendered hero. |
| `srcset` | `string` | `''` | Responsive candidates, passed through verbatim to the `<img>`. Serving a 2048px file into a 600px slot is one of the most common LCP mistakes, and this is the fix; pair with `sizes`. |
| `sizes` | `string` | `''` | `sizes` attribute — how wide the image renders at each breakpoint. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loaded` | `void` | Emits once the picture has finished loading. |
| `errored` | `void` | Emits when the picture fails to load and the fallback panel is shown. |

### MkImageCropper (component)

Selector: `mk-image-cropper` · exportAs: `mkImageCropper`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/media-manager

Import: `import { MkImageCropper } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

ImageCropper — pan-and-zoom crop control for avatars, covers and media uploads.
The image covers a fixed-aspect viewport (object-fit-cover style); the user
drags to pan, scrolls / pinch-zooms via the slider or `+`/`−` controls, and
`crop()` renders the visible region to a data-URL on an offscreen canvas.

Pan is always clamped so the image keeps covering the viewport, a
rule-of-thirds grid appears while dragging, and `round` overlays a circular
scrim for avatar crops (the exported bitmap stays rectangular). The crop
area is keyboard operable: Arrow keys pan by 10px (1px with Shift), `+`/`-`
zoom.

```html
<mk-image-cropper #cropper src="/assets/photo.jpg" [aspect]="1" round />
<button mkButton (click)="avatar = cropper.crop({ size: 512 })">Save</button>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` (required) | `string` |  | Image URL or data-URL to crop. |
| `aspect` | `number \| null` | `1` | Aspect ratio (width / height) of the crop viewport, e.g. `1` for a square or `16 / 9`. `null` makes the viewport fill its container. |
| `round` | `boolean` | `false` | Circular mask overlay for avatar crops. Purely visual — the exported bitmap from `crop()` stays rectangular. |
| `minZoom` | `number` | `1` | Lowest allowed zoom factor. |
| `maxZoom` | `number` | `4` | Highest allowed zoom factor. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable panning and zooming. |
| `crossOrigin` | `"anonymous" \| "use-credentials" \| null` | `null` | `crossorigin` for the internal `<img>`. Set to `'anonymous'` when cropping CORS-enabled remote images — without it the canvas is tainted and `crop()` returns `null`. Same-origin and data-URL sources don't need it. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string \| null` | `null` | Accessible name for the crop area (defaults to the i18n `zoom` label). |
| `zoom` (two-way) | `number` | `1` | Two-way zoom factor, clamped to `[minZoom, maxZoom]`. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `changed` | `void` | Emits on any pan or zoom change. |
| `imageError` | `void` | Emits when the image fails to load. |
| `zoomChange` | `number` | Emits when `zoom` changes (two-way binding). |

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `reset(): void` | Centre the image and reset zoom to 1 (clamped to `minZoom`). |
| `cropRect(): { sx: number; sy: number; sw: number; sh: number; } \| null` | The visible crop region in natural image pixels — what `crop()` would rasterise, without touching a canvas. Use it when the backend performs the actual crop from the master image (no client-side quality loss). Returns `null` until the image has loaded and the viewport is measured. |
| `crop(options?: { type?: string; quality?: number; size?: number; }): string \| null` |  |

### MkImageGallery (component)

Selector: `mk-image-gallery` · exportAs: `mkImageGallery`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/images

Import: `import { MkImageGallery } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Image gallery — a wall of clickable picture tiles built on `MkImage`.
Choose a uniform `grid`, a natural-ratio `masonry` flow, or a snap-scrolling
horizontal `strip`. Clicking a tile opens the shared `MkLightboxService`
at that picture (full-size `src`, not the thumb) and always emits
`itemClick`. With `max` set, only the first `max` tiles render and the last
one carries a "+N" overflow scrim that opens the rest in the lightbox.

```html
<mk-image-gallery
  [items]="[
    { src: '/photos/1.jpg', thumb: '/thumbs/1.jpg', alt: 'Harbour at dawn' },
    { src: '/photos/2.jpg', alt: 'Old town square', caption: 'Kraków' },
  ]"
  [columns]="4"
  [max]="8"
  aspectRatio="4 / 3"
  (itemClick)="onItemClick($event)"
/>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `readonly MkGalleryItem[]` |  | Pictures to show. |
| `layout` | `MkImageGalleryLayout` | `'grid'` | Tile arrangement. |
| `columns` | `number` | `3` | Grid/masonry column count; also sets the visible tile count of a strip. |
| `max` | `number \| null` | `null` | When set, show only the first `max` tiles plus a "+N" overflow tile. |
| `lightbox` | `boolean` | `true` | Open the shared lightbox on tile click. |
| `aspectRatio` | `string` | `'1 / 1'` | CSS aspect-ratio of grid/strip tiles (masonry keeps natural ratios). |
| `rounded` | `MkImageRounded` | `'md'` | Corner rounding of the tiles. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `itemClick` | `MkGalleryItemClick` | Emits on every tile click (also when the lightbox opens). |

### MkLightbox (component)

Selector: `mk-lightbox`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/images

Import: `import { MkLightbox } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Internal overlay component backing `MkLightboxService`. Renders the
current image near-fullscreen over the overlay scrim with a caption bar,
an `imageOf` counter, a close button and looping previous/next navigation.

Keyboard: `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` navigate, `Home`/`End` jump to the first
or last image. `Escape` and backdrop clicks are handled by the overlay
itself (`closeOnEscape` / `closeOnBackdropClick`), so they are deliberately
not re-handled here.

Open it via the service — not by placing `<mk-lightbox>` in a template:

```ts
inject(MkLightboxService).open(items, 2);
```

### MkMediaGallery (component)

Selector: `mk-media-gallery` · exportAs: `mkMediaGallery`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/media-manager

Import: `import { MkMediaGallery } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Media gallery — a management grid of image tiles for admin media libraries.
Each tile shows a square thumbnail (a labelled preview button emitting
`itemClick`), the item's name and optional meta line, an optional
selection checkbox (two-way `selection` model of selected ids) and an
optional consumer-projected action bar (`MkMediaActions`).

With `reorderable`, tiles become draggable via the dnd group's
`[mkDropList]` / `[mkDrag]` directives — pointer and keyboard dragging
(WCAG 2.1.1) both included. Each drop immutably updates the two-way `items`
model and emits `reordered`.

Clicking a tile always means "open/preview" — selection only toggles through
the checkbox, never on tile click.

```html
<mk-media-gallery
  [(items)]="assets"
  [(selection)]="selectedIds"
  selectable
  reorderable
  [columns]="5"
  (itemClick)="openPreview($event)"
  (reordered)="persistOrder($event)"
>
  <ng-template mkMediaActions let-item>
    <button mkButton size="sm" variant="ghost" (click)="edit(item)">Edit</button>
    <button mkButton size="sm" variant="ghost" tone="danger" (click)="remove(item)">
      Delete
    </button>
  </ng-template>
</mk-media-gallery>
```

Inputs:

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (two-way) | `MkMediaItem[]` | `[]` | The gallery's items (two-way). Replaced immutably on every reorder drop. |
| `selection` (two-way) | `string[]` | `[]` | Ids of the currently selected items (two-way). |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a selection checkbox on every tile. |
| `reorderable` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow drag-and-drop (pointer + keyboard) reordering of the tiles. |
| `columns` | `number` | `4` | Number of grid columns. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `this.i18n.mediaLibrary` | Accessible name of the gallery region. Defaults to `i18n.mediaLibrary`. |

Outputs:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `itemsChange` | `MkMediaItem[]` | Emits when `items` changes (two-way binding). |
| `selectionChange` | `string[]` | Emits when `selection` changes (two-way binding). |
| `itemClick` | `MkMediaItem` | Emitted when a tile's preview button is activated (click/Enter/Space). |
| `reordered` | `MkMediaReorderEvent` | Emitted after a drop has updated the `items` model. |

### MkMediaActions (directive)

Selector: `[mkMediaActions]`

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/media-manager

Import: `import { MkMediaActions } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Marks an `<ng-template>` as the per-tile action bar for `MkMediaGallery`.
The template's implicit context is the `MkMediaItem`, so consumers can
destructure it with `let-item`. The gallery renders it into each tile's
top-right action bar (revealed on hover / focus-within, always visible on
touch devices); the consumer supplies the buttons and their handlers.

```html
<mk-media-gallery [items]="assets()">
  <ng-template mkMediaActions let-item>
    <button mkButton size="sm" variant="ghost" (click)="edit(item)">Edit</button>
  </ng-template>
</mk-media-gallery>
```

Properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `template` | `TemplateRef<{ $implicit: MkMediaItem; }>` | The projected action-bar template, rendered once per tile. |

### MkLightboxService (service)

Docs: https://mk-kit.dev/components/images

Import: `import { MkLightboxService } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Fullscreen image lightbox — opens a set of images in a modal overlay with
looping previous/next navigation, captions, a counter, keyboard support
(Arrow keys, Home/End, Escape) and focus trapping, all powered by
`MkOverlayService`.

```ts
private readonly lightbox = inject(MkLightboxService);

viewPhoto(index: number): void {
  this.lightbox.open(
    [
      { src: '/photos/1.jpg', alt: 'Harbour at dawn', caption: 'Dawn' },
      { src: '/photos/2.jpg', alt: 'Old town square' },
    ],
    index,
  );
}
```

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `open(items: readonly MkLightboxItem[], startIndex?: number): void` | Open the lightbox over the page. Does nothing when `items` is empty. `startIndex` is clamped into `[0, items.length - 1]`. |

### mkClampPan (function)

Import: `import { mkClampPan } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Clamp a pan offset (CSS px, measured from the viewport centre to the image
centre) so the image scaled by `scale` still covers the viewport — no empty
edges. When the scaled image is not larger than the viewport on an axis the
offset collapses to `0` (centred).

```ts
function mkClampPan(x: number, y: number, imgW: number, imgH: number, vpW: number, vpH: number, scale: number): { x: number; y: number; }
```

### mkCoverScale (function)

Import: `import { mkCoverScale } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Base cover scale for an image in a viewport — the smallest scale at which
`imgW × imgH` fully covers `vpW × vpH` (object-fit: cover). Returns `1`
for degenerate (non-positive) dimensions.

```ts
function mkCoverScale(imgW: number, imgH: number, vpW: number, vpH: number): number
```

### mkCropRect (function)

Import: `import { mkCropRect } from '@mk-kit/ui/media';`

Source rect (in natural image pixels) of the crop region visible through
the viewport. `scale` maps natural pixels to CSS pixels (cover scale ×
zoom); `panX`/`panY` are the CSS-px offsets of the image centre from the
viewport centre. The rect is clamped inside the image bounds.

```ts
function mkCropRect(imgNaturalW: number, imgNaturalH: number, vpW: number, vpH: number, scale: number, panX: number, panY: number): { sx: number; sy: number; sw: number; sh: number; }
```

### MkHarness (class)

and expose user-level actions (`click()`, `selectOption()`, …) and reads
(`isChecked()`, `text()`), so specs never depend on the component's DOM.

| `isRequired(): boolean` |  |
| `isFocused(): boolean` |  |

### MkMenuHarness (class)

Import: `import { MkMenuHarness } from '@mk-kit/ui/testing';`

A `[mkMenuTriggerFor]` trigger and the `mk-menu` panel it opens. The host
is matched by the trigger's `aria-haspopup="menu"` (the directive's
attribute is an input binding, so it is not in the DOM).

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `isOpen(): boolean` |  |
| `open(): Promise<void>` |  |
| `close(): Promise<void>` |  |
| `panel(): MkTestElement \| null` | The teleported panel (`[role="menu"]`), or `null` while closed. |
| `items(): Promise<string[]>` | Item texts of the open menu (opens it if needed). Submenu panels excluded. |
| `clickItem(which: number \| string \| RegExp): Promise<void>` | Click an item by index, exact text or RegExp (opens the menu first). |
| `isItemDisabled(which: number \| string \| RegExp): Promise<boolean>` |  |

### MkTestElement (class)

Import: `import { MkTestElement } from '@mk-kit/ui/testing';`

A DOM element wrapped for tests: reads are synchronous, every interaction
dispatches the same events a user would and then settles change detection
(`fixture.detectChanges()` + `whenStable()`), so the next read sees the
updated view.

Methods:

| Signature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `text(): string` | Trimmed text content with whitespace collapsed. |
| `attr(name: string): string \| null` |  |
| `hasClass(name: string): boolean` |  |
| `prop<T = unknown>(name: string): T` | Read a DOM property (`value`, `checked`, `open`, …). |
| `matches(selector: string): boolean` |  |
| `isFocused(): boolean` |  |
| `isDisabled(): boolean` | Native `disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"` or a `--disabled` host class. |
| `query(selector: string): MkTestElement \| null` |  |
| `queryAll(selector: string): MkTestElement[]` |  |
| `child(selector: string): MkTestElement` | Like `query`, but throws a readable error when nothing matches. |
| `click(): Promise<void>` | pointerdown → mousedown → focus → pointerup → mouseup → click, like a user. |
| `hover(): Promise<void>` |  |
| `leave(): Promise<void>` |  |
| `focus(): Promise<void>` |  |
| `blur(): Promise<void>` |  |
| `type(text: string): Promise<void>` | Type into an input/textarea/contenteditable character by character — keydown, `value` append, `input`, keyup — then settle. Use `setValue` to replace the value in one go. |
| `setValue(value: string): Promise<void>` | Set the value of an input/textarea/select and fire `input` + `change`. |
| `clear(): Promise<void>` |  |
| `sendKeys(...keys: Array<MkTestKey \| (string & {})>): Promise<void>` | Dispatch keydown/keyup for each key. Printable single characters are also typed. |
| `dispatch(event: Event): Promise<void>` | Dispatch any event on the element and settle. |


### MkHarnessFilters (interface)

Import: `import { MkHarnessFilters } from '@mk-kit/ui/testing';`

Filters every harness lookup accepts. `selector` narrows the host elements
considered (e.g. a class or attribute your template sets); `text` matches
the host's trimmed text content — a string must match exactly, a RegExp
is tested.

Members:

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selector`? | `string \| undefined` |  |
| `text`? | `string \| RegExp \| undefined` |  |

| Name | Type | Description |

### MkTestKey (type)

Import: `import { MkTestKey } from '@mk-kit/ui/testing';`

Keys accepted by `MkTestElement.sendKeys` besides printable characters.

```ts
type MkTestKey = | 'Enter' | 'Escape' | 'Tab' | 'Backspace' | 'Delete' | ' ' | 'ArrowUp' | 'ArrowDown' | 'ArrowLeft' | 'ArrowRight' | 'Home' | 'End' | 'PageUp' | 'PageDown';
```
